title: Every 2π the Same! Periodicity Explained Simply | PUC Maths Class 11
description:
A heart monitor draws a spike, then the same spike again, and again. Diya sees one in a biology video and thinks of the sine wave: both repeat. But how long is one repeat of sin x, and why does it repeat at all? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 3, Trigonometric Functions) we meet periodicity and the mirror symmetry of the trigonometric graphs.

You will watch P keep turning round the unit circle while y = sin x prints the same wave again every 2pi, prove sin(2n pi + x) = sin x in four steps, see why tan x repeats every pi, and watch the cosine graph fold along the y-axis and the sine graph spin half a turn about the origin: cos(-x) = cos x and sin(-x) = -sin x. Two pause-and-think questions, a worked example (sin of -1050 degrees with a live clockwise spin), the exam trap about sin(-x), an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and JEE Main students.

In this video:
0:00 A heartbeat that repeats
0:27 Live: keep turning, the wave prints again
0:54 Proof: sin(2n pi + x) = sin x
1:31 Tangent repeats every pi
1:43 2pi vs pi: side by side
2:14 Symmetry: cos(-x) and sin(-x)
3:20 Worked example: sin(-1050 degrees)
3:56 Exam trap: sin(-x) is not sin x
4:12 Where it is asked
4:19 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
